meaning: The number of brave warriors from the tribe of Simeon who joined David in Hebron (1 Chron. 12:26).
description: The number 7100 appears in 1 Chronicles 12:26, where it is stated that seven thousand one hundred brave warriors from the tribe of Simeon came to Hebron to make David king over all Israel. The context is the great gathering of tribal warriors who recognized David's kingship after Saul's death. Although 7100 does not have a broad independent symbolic tradition, it carries the resonances of its components: the number 7, which symbolizes perfection and divine wholeness, and 100, which expresses fullness and completeness. In this context, the number emphasizes that Simeon's contribution to David's army was significant and complete.

versions.meaning: The number 7100 has no established symbolic meaning in biblical or Jewish tradition.
versions.description: The number 7100 does not appear as a specific symbolic number in the Bible or in traditional Jewish numerology. Although the components 7 (perfection/holiness) and 100 (fullness/completeness) each have known symbolic meanings, there is no recognized tradition that assigns the combination 7100 its own symbolic significance. It is also not associated with any known gematria value of theological importance.

The context is the great gathering of tribal warriors who recognized David's kingship after Saul's death. Although 7100 does not have a broad independent symbolic tradition, it carries the resonances of its components: the number 7, which symbolizes perfection and divine wholeness, and 100, which expresses fullness and completeness. footnotes.text: 1 Chron. 12:23–40 lists the armed forces from each tribe who came to David in Hebron. Simeon's contribution of 7,100 men was among the smaller contingents, compared for example with Judah (6,800) and Zebulun (50,000).
The tribe of Simeon had its inheritance within the territory of Judah (Josh. 19:1–9), which may explain their early loyalty to David, who himself belonged to the tribe of Judah.

In rabbinic tradition, the listing in 1 Chron. 12 is seen as a testimony to God's guidance in gathering all Israel under one king, where each tribal contribution reflects the character and role of that tribe.

footnotes.text: 1 Chron. 12:23–40 lists the armed forces from each tribe who came to David in Hebron. Simeon's contribution of 7,100 men was modest compared with the largest contingents, such as Zebulun (50,000) and Naphtali (37,000), yet still larger than for example Judah's 6,800.
The tribe of Simeon had its inheritance within the territory of Judah (Josh. 19:1–9), which may explain their early loyalty to David, who himself belonged to the tribe of Judah.

In rabbinic tradition, the listing in 1 Chron. 12 is seen as a testimony to God's guidance in gathering all Israel under one king, where each tribal contribution reflects the character and role of that tribe.
